newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks push higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks push higher at close.

text.p: Strength in stocks listed abroad pulled the Argentine stock market back into positive territory Monday and near-term prospects remain good, traders said.
"The market remains confident and today the motor behind the rise were the ADR stocks, which had been lagging the (blue-chip) MerVal index recently," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The MerVal jumped 1.0 percent to close at 609.28, recouping Friday's slim loss. The index rallied 4.1 percent last week.
"The market's resistance level is 618-620, but it could benefit from a correction earlier," Npoli said.

Brokers noted sentiment was underpinned by strong economic fundamentals and a calmer political front after the row sparked last month by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's accusations of government-linked corruption.
However, the enabling factor for local gains was the performance of the New York markets.
"The drop in the past two weeks of the (U.S.) long bond yield has allowed our market to recover and take advantage of the economic recovery," another trader said.
The broad market tacked on 1.3 percent Monday, with winners beating losers 40 to 13 and 17 issues closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 20.6 million pesos from 18.6 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals dipped to 105.2 million pesos from 107.6 million Friday.

The main-tier standout was oil firm Sol Petroleo, up 6.5 percent. Petrochemical firm Indupa and Telefnica jumped 3.9 percent and 3.2 percent respectively, while Telecom rose 1.5 percent and oil giant YPF rose 1.7 percent. The only loser was construction stock Polledo, off 1.0 percent on buyout rumors.
